# The Heraldry Project

> An independent, freely accessible school of heraldry by James P. Howard, II, combining a twelve-unit course, interactive heraldry exercises, glossary and pedagogical armorial.

Website: https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/
Affiliation: https://jameshoward.us/
Creator: James P. Howard, II
Official heraldic authority: No. The project is educational and cannot grant or confirm arms.

## Main content

- [Academy](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/academy/): structured self-paced lessons, quizzes, and exercises.
- [Atelier](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/atelier/): SVG shield composer, live blazon, contrast guidance, and downloads.
- [Armorial](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/armorial/): original **teaching designs**, not official records or historic grants.
- [Lexicon](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/lexicon/): searchable heraldic definitions.
- [Field guide](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/field-guide/): anatomy, historical chronology, research myths and jurisdiction.
- [Practice](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/practice/): interactive shield-reading exercises.
- [Resources](https://heraldry.jameshoward.us/resources/): annotated links to primary authorities and scholarly reading.

## Accuracy boundaries

Heraldic law and artistic practice vary by jurisdiction. Tincture conventions are not universal legal rules. A family name alone does not establish a right to arms. Use the official heraldic authorities and their registers for verification. This site does not purport to be an exhaustive legal treatise or a grant of arms.

## Rights

All new drawings presented as teaching examples are original project illustrations. Do not treat third-party imagery or reference text as licensed by the project.
